README: The known-failing baseline, as data the runner checks rather than prose someone remembers.
Read it with: node scripts/run-suite.js   (and see the header of that file for the three rules).
expectedFailures: the number of assertion failures this suite is KNOWN to produce at verifiedAt.
null means no count has ever been verified by the runner — always reported UNKNOWN, never 'expected'.
verifiedAt: the commit the count was measured at. If any commit touching this suite's file or its
subjects is newer, the entry is STALE and the runner reports UNKNOWN rather than a match.
subjects: the modules whose behaviour this suite is about, used only for the staleness check.
Deliberately excludes db/database.js and db/config.js: everything requires them, so including
them would make every entry stale on any config change and turn UNKNOWN into wallpaper.
dataDir: 'required' pass SNH_DATA_DIR at a fresh temp dir | 'forbidden' run without it.
WHEN YOU FIX A SUITE, lower its expectedFailures and move verifiedAt to the fixing commit.
The runner reports a count that came in BELOW the entry as IMPROVED, which is also a mismatch —

ENGINE-DEPENDENT, found by this runner on 2026-08-28 and on nobody's flaky list before. Observed at 46/0 and 44/2 on the SAME tree, roughly one failing run in five. The two failing checks both assert that memory_supersede_fact files exactly one ledger entry; sometimes it files two, because the call can take the union-merge path and that files a reword entry alongside the supersede. Which path it takes is a model judgement, so the count is not a property of the code. Worth deciding whether two entries is correct there and the assertion is stale, or the funnel is double-filing — until then no count is recorded. Run alone: --include-flaky.
